summary: Possible GitHub Actions secret exfiltration via phishing redirect targeting developer CI token
description: Issue summary: A developer reported an unexpected approval prompt from a GitHub Actions workflow after clicking a link in an external email. The link redirected to a third-party page that requested a GitHub OAuth reauthorization. The developer completed the flow using their corporate SSO (Okta), after which we observed an unusual spike in CI-triggered deploy jobs and new runner labels appearing in the org. Impact: Potential exfiltration or misuse of GITHUB_TOKEN-like secrets or third-party app tokens created during the OAuth flow. No confirmed data leakage yet, but CI pipelines ran on branches with privileged deploy steps. Environment: production GitHub org (redwood-inference), GitHub Actions runners (self-hosted and GH-hosted), corporate SSO via Okta, developer laptop (macOS, corporate-managed). Timeline: 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC - developer receives external email with link; 09:18 UTC - developer clicks link and completes OAuth reauth; 09:22 UTC - spike of CI workflows started across unrelated repos; 09:24 UTC - security alert triggered by anomalous runner label creation; 09:30 UTC - developer opens internal support and Security notified. Steps to reproduce (observed flow): 1) Malicious email contains link to staging.redwood-assets.com/gh-auth?redirect=... 2) Link redirects to github.com/login/oauth/authorize with a client_id matching a third-party app (app id matches a public vendor account) 3) OAuth consent screen shows organization-level scopes (workflow, repo) 4) Developer approves via Okta SSO 5) New personal access-like token or app installation leads to CI runs. Observed logs: - Audit log entries: oauth_authorization.created (client_id: 5f4a3b, scopes: repo, workflow) - Actions logs: multiple repository_dispatch and workflow_dispatch events initiated from IPs in EU region not associated with our CI pool - Runner registration events: new runner label "temp-uk-12" associated with self-hosted pool, token used from unknown host. Initial hypotheses: a malicious third-party OAuth app used a phishing redirect to request org-level workflow access and a service token was issued (or a token-equivalent app installation). Alternatively, the flow could have leveraged a consent phishing page that swapped client_id after redirect. Immediate risk: execution of privileged deploy workflows and access to secrets provided to Actions contexts. Recommended immediate mitigations executed: 1) Revoked all recent OAuth authorizations issued around 2026-03-10 09:00-10:00 UTC. 2) Rotated repository-level secrets used by deploy workflows (CI_DEPLOY_KEY, PROD_DB_DSN). 3) Disabled self-hosted runner registration and removed suspicious runners. 4) Temporarily set Actions permissions to read-only where possible and limited workflows with deploy permissions. Next steps (pending): run audit across org for other new OAuth apps, review Okta login events for the developer, collect dev laptop forensic snapshot, verify whether any secrets were exfiltrated from workflow logs or artifacts.

investigation_notes: Initial containment appears successful: OAuth grants revoked, secrets rotated, and suspicious runners removed. Still investigating whether the OAuth flow resulted in an app installation granting persistent access or a one-time token used to trigger workflows. Audit logs show org-level oauth_authorization with repo+workflow scopes; need to correlate token usage to run IDs. Okta logs show the developer's SSO session originated from their corp IP at 09:18 UTC. No outbound data transfer to unknown endpoints from GH-hosted runners found so far. Artefacts and workflow logs scan in progress (pattern scan for secrets).
resolution: In progress - mitigations applied (revoked OAuth grants, rotated secrets, removed runners, limited Actions permissions). Follow-up items: full org OAuth sweep, CI artifact review, user education email on consent phishing, update runbook to require security approval for org-level app consent. Will update when root cause confirmed or when containment completed.
